activities.title: My language
activities.content:
Teach a rule of the language
• Say: Tsuun pëkuanju tsi utsia pëfootu pëcak, iink. 
• Unjär woom ci wën wi? [Aci uyët].
• Point to the next picture in the row, to the right of 
the bull.
• Say: "Ngëtsu pëkuanj inja tsi pëfootu pëcak. Tsum  
a naam ni pëcints pun? Nin!"
• Point to the next picture in the row. 
• Say: "Ngëteen pëfootu pëcints pun. Tsum a naam ni pëcak pun? Nin!"
• Point to the final picture in the row. 
• Say: "Tsum pi anaam ni pëfootu pëcak pun? Ee-e!"
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
illustration and find the other illustration in the row that matches.
Compare shapes
• Ask pupils to turn to the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Use the same process as the activity above with the shapes on the next page of the Pupil Book.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: "Tsuun pëkuanju tsi utsia pëfootu pëcak. We wi iñaan ni këro wun?"
• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what the 
people are doing in each picture and ask questions to help them think about the pictures.
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling. Help them see 
that the woman is preparing "Bëmaaj".

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say:"We wi napats niints ni di pëfootu këro wën. Ngëtëkul nu kob pëboola kaniajan! Nda 
paarir a? Tsuun pëkuanj u këpiban-naan bëga pëboola."
• Show pupils how to trace the line from the ball to the goal with a finger.
• Say: "We wi ucatsa ci wën tsi përo? We wi mwejats wën ne ucatsa aŋal?
• Watch as pupils trace the line from the monkey to the banana with a finger.
• Repeat with the remaining image.

activities.title: Parts of a Book
activities.content:
Recognize the Grade parts of a book - cover, 
back,title. Point to the cover and back of a book
• Say: Nja ka teen kafëlal pëkur ni bërun te di 
bëfets..Kii ci kun kafëlal kacäk ti ubuk.
• Irim inci yi di bërun kafëlal kacäk tsi ubuk, ka 
leents inja ubiban-naani ubuk. Upiban-naani ka 
leentsu ko wi kii win wi di kafëlal.
• "Uband inja tsi katëtan bat i, nja kawin bëfets 
ubuk.

activities.title: Vocabulary – Before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils what 
they know about each one.
Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If needed, 
help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know
Lillaants; Pëjúk; Tsënku

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available.
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments such as 
when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learned.
ALBETINA ABUER PËTIINKËTS
Albetina lilaants. Aci di kato te kaats ko wi nuu ro wi. A na win asinul ŋaats, Yama, ci tsi kajant m 
maaj. A na jaul, paapu ŋaants, mán tsënku-a? Oo nin! Albetina, m cësara ume. A na pën atsëp.
Albetina win ayiëtul këgijëlän iwusi. Tsëmak iñaan, mán tsënku-a. Oo nin! Albetina, m cësara ume. 
A na pën atsëp.
A na win tsëmakul niints di kasël kakul. Tsëmak iñaan, mán tsënku-a. Oo nin! Albetina, m cësara 
ume. A na pën atsëp.
U cints, a na win tsëmakul ŋaats ktsi karo uleemp ikol. Tsëmak iñaan, mán tsënku-a. Oo nin! 
Albetina, m cësara ume.
Din, a na tsëp di asinul. A asinul yeparul, Albetina, we wi mjuatsan wën?
" Man cësara ume uci jant m maaj; Man cësara ume uci gijëlän iwusi; Man m cësara ume uci sël 
kakul; Man m cësara ume uci do uleepm ikol. Inkri, we wi ka wën përo?
A asinul jaul, o Albetina, cats juatsan, kawiakau aling. Man fiër iñan yi kantsënkin yi pëtsu mleele 
di iwusi. Këtsëkin-a? A Albetina tsënkul.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review the parts of a book - cover, back, title
• Call on a volunteer pupil to show the class which part of a book you start reading from. Ask 
what this part of the book it is called. (correct response: ("front page")
• Say: Tsum ti m wii-na tsum upiban-naani katëtan? ("Tsi bërun kalëmi ubuk.""
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer. Call on a second volunteer pupil to say the title of the 
story that was just read aloud.
• Say: Uband inja bëfet ubuk, we wi nja këwin wën? ("Bëfets kalëmi ubuk.")
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer and point to the back of the book.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare shapes of capital letters 
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the 
page and point to the first capital letter. Do not say 
the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for 
pupils to learn letters. It is an activity for pupils to 
practice telling the difference between letter and 
shapes.
• Say : "Mán  yuer pëkuanj inji tsi uwab ucäk. Iñaan kaats pëyuër pëkuanjul tul. Nja kee tsas 
ulon un naam win ni wël."
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: "Ngëtu pëkuanj inja tsi uwab ucäk. Tsum a naam ni ucäk? Nin!"
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say:  Ngëteen ucints wën.Tsum a naam ni ucäk wën?
• Point to the final one in the row.
• Say: Tsum wi a naam ni ucak wën? Ee-e!
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
capital letter and find the other one in the row that matches it.
Compare shapes
• Use the same process as the activity above with the small letters on the next page of the Pupil 
Book. Do not say the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for pupils to learn letters. It is 
an activity for pupils to practice telling the difference between letter shapes.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the four objects in the next activity. Ask pupils to 
point to the objects in their own books.
• Call on pupils to describe what images go together and why (there is no 1 correct answer).

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Say: Ngëfetsan ngëjarabuts ngi. Ucäk wën aci usuel! Ngëtsu pëkuanj inja di unjuundi ja ka  
fetsan bëga bi uu cat bi di kafëlal.
• Demonstrate following the line on the page as needed.
• Repeat with the remaining images.
• Uja wi, apëni di katëtan ki ndonki teenar-ind di kafëlal

activities.title: Words are separated by spaces
activities.content:
Describe what a word is, and why there are spaces 
between them
• Take out the read aloud book from yesterday's 
lesson. 
• Choose a sentence to write on the board.
• Say: Uja wi, apëni di katëtan ki ndon ki teenarind di kafëlal
• Nja ka ñakan-naan undo tsëko tsan citsi di incuaf irim
• Mán nja ndunteen kafëlal, ka teen-na përim pëloole pëloole. Përim pan ci pi aka ko wi pa pac 
wi.
• Point to a word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Point to the space after the word.
• Say: "Tsëko tsan ci tsi tsi pëncuaf irim , a piban-in tsi përim nats tsi ni tsi pëcints kur tsi. 
• Point to the following word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Say: Tsëko tsan ci ti di pëncuaf irim, katsënku këpurir pëteen kafëlal. Uci m pican ngëja nga 
pats gi, këfiër tsëko tsi kan ci tsi di pëcuaf irim.
• Write another sentence. Choose a volunteer to help demonstrate on the new sentence.
• Say: "Tsuun pëkuanj di utsia përim. Inkri, piban-nin përim pëcints. Um di këpiban dun ne kërim 
• këtëb ki naamats? (Tsëko ci tsi pëncuaf yul.)
• Pick up the book. Walk around the room. Ask 3 pupils to find a space between two words, and 
put their fingers on it.

activities.title: Read sight words
activities.content:
Learn two new sight words
• Point to the pictures of the boy and girl in the Pupil 
Book.
• Say: Ni ci un Abi. Ni ci un Abi. Nja ka teen ngëko 
• ngëcumal di kafëlal undo bukul tsi uwal pëjuk wi. 
• Say: Say: "Tsuun pëkuanj di utsia përim Abi, tsi utsia pëfootu napäts niints. Tsuun pënkuanj di 
utsia përim Abi, tsi utsia pëfootu napäts ŋaats."
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (matching activity).
• Ask pupils to point to [ Abi] on the left side, then point to the matching name on the right side. 
Repeat with [ Abi].
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (box with boy and girl names).
• Ask pupils to say the first name in the left column, then point to the matching name in the row.
• Continue in the same way with each row.

activities.title: Read a sentence
activities.content:
Read a sentence using sight words
• Say: Ma win Abi di ruets kafëlal ki. A win buts përim pëwalu. Përim pëwalu pi aja "Teenan". 
• Parme ngëme Abi, a ngëme buts përim pëwalu pi, nja ka purir pëteen kafëlal nja kame ko wi 
• ifootu yi ja wi.
• Point to the first picture sentence on the page in the Pupil Book. Ask pupils to name the 
picture on the right.
• Read the picture sentence aloud to pupils, showing them how you point to the pictures/word 
with your finger as you read.
• Continue to the next picture sentence. Ask pupils to point to the boy.
• Point to pictures or words as you read. Abi a win upi
• Remind pupils that "Pëteen" means "to observe" or "pëwin" to see."
• "• "

• Make a gesture to demonstrate seeing. Then, ask pupils to read the picture sentence again 
together.
• Say: Inkri yën ni m win un tsi utsia tsi? Ngëtsu ikuanj inja tsi uja wi nja ka teen kafëlal tsëloole. 
[ Abi a win untabul]
• Say: Yën purirun pëja uja ucints wi?
• Continue calling on pupils to read the picture sentences until the end of the page.

activities.title: How to read – track with a finger
activities.content:
Teach how to track words with a finger 
• Say: Mán nja ndunteen kafëlal, ka teen-na përim 
pëloole pëloole. Përim pan ci pi aka ko wi pa pac wi. 
Pëme ko wi këteen wi di kafëlal, ape pëwara pëteen 
na përim pan ci pi. Pëtsu pëkuanj tsi utsia përim 
pan ci pi uwal wi këteen wi kafëlal, ka tsënku m dits 
lut përim..
• Write a sentence on the board. Demonstrate how to track with your finger under each word as 
you read. Be sure to place and pause your finger under the specific word.
• Call on a pupil at random to describe what to do with a finger while reading.
• Call on 2 pupils to demonstrate tracking words of the sentence on the board while you read it 
aloud.

activities.content:

Ajuabëts,   Nacuunkan,  Iyësats.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud 
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available
• Partway through the story, pause to show pupils how you track reading with your finger below 
each word you read as you read it. At the end of the line of text, make a big sweeping motion 
back to the start of the next line of text. Continue tracking with your finger.
• After demonstrating, complete the read aloud.

ADAMA A MAAK UKAFAL
Adama, aci ni aninul ni asinul. Aninul ni asinul ruul, "Adama!" Kato juabëts. Bu teets iñaan jaankëma. 
Adama aci tsum?
Adam ate bi anin këruwar bi. Adam ate bi asin këruwar bi. Adama jankëmaatsa. Adama piints di 
bëkaab rin.
A anin ni asin teenëlär. Anin tukar pëfër Adama.
A aninul du kak, Adama, bëfa. Koroom? Adama jankëma, "O, yaaya, iyësats!Aninul tsu kañanul 
tsi pëjuk Adama a na ja, "Uliafu a yëkan!" Mán dui nacuunkan!" Asinul tsëp përui nacuunkan di 
utelefoŋ. Nacuunkan bi ee teen Adama a na ja, "Uliafu ayëkan! Ngëcuunkan pëmaaku!"
Ipës Adama are mak a na ja, "Nacuunkan, nacuunkan! Mán cats-a?" A nacuunkan ji a na jaul, "Nin, 
Adama! Mán wëlu bëko këŋooi!"
Aninul ja, "Nacuunkan, baran! A nacuunkan ja bukul,"Ind tsëfin undo bëko. Pëpën tsi ntsari,, 
Adama a ka puu piints di unteenda untsua wi bëko!"
Aninul teen asinul a na ja, "Ngëweel unteenda wi ntsari! Jampësan, tukari kanëm ucar!" Adama te 
bi bu këñakan bi a na piints.
Ko wi anaam ni katëtan abi pëpiban bi nja kërand bi pëmaak ni pëcuunkan pul, pëliincan buts pëtsas 
bëcuunkan ni pëpiints di unteenda un tsua wi bëko.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in their own 
words.
• Say: Inkri, ngëjej irim yi ngëjuk yi nja ka leempna yul uja.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil 
book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a 
new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the 
pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review tracking words with a finger
• Ask a volunteer pupil to tell you something you should do to be sure you don't skip words while 
reading. (Correct response - track the words with your finger, or follow under the words with 
your finger, etc.)
• Ask one pupil to demonstrate tracking for the class using the book.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Who" (Yën" ")
• Read the question: 
• Say: Yën dui-un nacuukan bi Adama maak bi? ( Asin Adama dui-un nacuukan bi Adama maak 
• bi).
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word " Yën" is asking about. Call on one or 
two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word "yën" asks us the name of a someone or something alive)
• Teach pupils to use the question word  "Tsum"
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, " Tsum" Tell pupils that they will 
use it to answer the next question.
• Read the question: 
• Say: Uwal wi m maak wi, tsum tsi m ja tsun m ndoo këtsëp?
• Say: "Përim 'tsum' ka tsu inja ja ka jaakëmaana uleka tsëko oo ko undo wi. Man ja te 'tsum' 
• kame ne ujaakëma ka ci undo tsëko.  
• Read the question: 
• Say: Tsum tsi Adama doon tsu ci uwal wi aninul ni asinul këruul wi? (Adama a ro ci di pëfërul 
• uwal wi asinul ni aninul këruul wi).
• Say: Ngë maban ngëwejats inja tsi tsëko tsi ngëteen tsi di kafëlal. Kafëlal aja inja ne na ko ro 
• wama piints di bëkaab.
• Ask pupils to think about "where", or the place, that this happened.
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: Tsum tsi asin Adama weel-na tsun unteenda? (Asin Adama aweeel-na 
• unteenda di kanëm).
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. Remind pupils that it is a "where" question.
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

• Say: Përim poom pi m yëkërän pun, payepar pi undo tsëko oo undo ko undolaa wi?
• Call on a pupil at random who raised their hand. Remind them that the word is "Tsum "

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Display mastery of key skills learned over the last four lessons: the parts of a book, spaces between words and tracking a finger under print.

activities.title: Assessment
activities.content:
Special assessment - assess week 1 skills:
1. Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book 
means.
2. Understand that words in print are separated by 
spaces
3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps 
keep track of where you are reading.
1. Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book means
• Hand out pupil books
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "front". Give feedback and explain. Give 
more examples if needed. If you see any pupil struggling, make sure to support them in this 
skill during the next lessons.
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "back" of the book. Give feedback, and 
explain and give more examples if needed. 
2. Understand that words in print are separated by spaces
• Ask pupils to turn to the first decodable story in their book. Show them the picture for the 
story, so they can find the story in the book. They will not be able to read this story yet, but 
that is alright. Do not ask them to read the story.
• Point to the "space" between the first two words in the story. Ask all pupils to put their finger 
on that space. Walk around and show them where to put their finger.
• Ask pupils to point to the next space in the story. Walk around to observe and give feedback.
• Ask pupils to raise their hand if they know what that space is for (why it's there). 
• Ask a volunteer to answer. Ask another pupil if the response is correct.
• Say: Uwaanta un ci wi tsi pëncuaf irim, a piban ne kërim këtëb ki a pats.
3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps keep track of where you are reading
• Open a big book (any big book) to the first page. Ask pupils to watch and listen. Read the first 
sentence while pointing to (tracking) each word with your finger.
• Ask pupils what you were doing with your finger. Then ask them why you did that. Tell the 
pupil who responds if they are correct or not. Then repeat or say the correct response. 
(Possible response: I was tracking a finger under the words as I read them. Tracking with a 
finger helps you know where you are while reading, so you don't get confused or lost.).

turn back to that page in the Pupil Book and repeat that activity.

1. Draw lines and shapes
2. Read sentences with sight words
3. Choose the letter that matches the first letter in the row
4. Recognize sight words (character names)

• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling.

activities.title: Read a sentence using sight words
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to independently read the picture sentences using the sight words they learned 
yesterday. Walk around the room to monitor and help pupils as needed. Ensure that pupils are 
reading from left to right and tracking the pictures/words with their finger.
• After giving pupils an opportsumity to read the sentences, call on pupils at random to read 
aloud the first 6 picture sentences.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Identify and say the target vowel sound and recognize the letter that represents that sound.
Hear and recognize in writing the difference between the short and long vowel sound.
Write the letter.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the Letter
• Point to the lowercase letter /a/ on the alphabet 
poster or on the board.
• Say: Wi ci wën uwab inja uwalu ntsari. Bëruur 
• uwab wi aci /a/. Ngëja /a/.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the uppercase letter "A" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Uwab wi aci uloole wën.Bëruur wël aci buts /a/.Uci ujuund-na uja oo katim, nja ka win 
• upicänaa iink /A/.
• Point to the lowercase letter "a" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ngëwal ngëcumal, nja ka win upicänaa iink tsi irim /a/.
• Say: Uwab "a", aci bëruur bëkaats un ci wi uwab umpats wi tsi ngëwab. Nja kee juk mak bëruur
• ngëwab ngëkaats tsi inëm yi kam bi yi. Ape pëwara uci ngëme bëruur ngëwab ngëkaats parme 
• ngëko ka winaa tsi përim pan ci pi uci këteen kafëlal.

activities.title: Teach pupils to hear syllables
activities.content:
Clap two-syllable words
• Say: M purir pëpatsës përim ka ro itawar. Katawar kan ci ki a tsij bëruur uwab ukaats,bi 
ngëron bi juk ba /a/, /te/. Ngëwaaf nja ka teen. "ate"
•  Model by clapping:  →a  /te /
• Practice together with pupils:  WORD→  SYLLABLES  / /,  WORD→  SYLLABLES  Ate: /a/te/
• Pupils practice alone: WORD→  SYLLABLES  / /, WORD→  SYLLABLES  / /Ate:  /a/te/
• Clap words with different numbers of syllables
• Say: Irim yi aka bëruur ngëyaas ngëtëb, maa përim apurir pëka bëruur bëloole, bëruur 
ngëwaants, 
• ni pëpe.Ngëteen irim ilon ko utiis. Mán cäkës nja përim. Inkri nja ka waaf bëlieng ngëyaas 
• ngëtëb.

• Words:  Aba: /a/ba/; kakani: /ka/ka/ni/

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: We wi m win wën?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help pupils 
understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Ngëwaaf bëruur ngan ci ngi tsi përim (paapa). Ngëyaas um ngi m te ngun bëruur uwab/a/ tsi 
• përim (paapa)? Ngëwaaf kak.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the sound, help 
them by saying another word with that sound in your language or another language they know.
• Say: Ngëja bëlieng përim pëcints- (mama). Tsum m te bëruur uwab ukaats /a/ tsi përim(mama)? 
• Ngëyaas um ngi m te ngun wël?
• Say: Inkri aci uwal ind. Nda jaan përim. Uja ind pul, nda tsuun pëkuanj tsi utsia uwab /a/ uwal wi 
• nda ru wi /a/.
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Nja bëlieng ngëtu pëkuanj di utsia pëfootu pan pic pi "bëkaab " di utsia pul.
• Say: We wi nda win wën? Aci "bëkaab".
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: Bëruur /a/ apurir pëci bëyampal. Pac wën ne uci nja këru wël, nja ka tsiisan pëtsu wël 
• U yamp. Tsum m te bëruur uwab /aa/ utsiisan, tsi përim "bëkaab?"
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the same 
vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to each other. 
Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two /a/ together, it makes a long sound /aa/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long (stretched) 
sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the syllables 
and listen for the long vowel in the word.

activities.title: Writing – Letter
activities.content:
Write the letter and say its sound
• Write the letter /a/ on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm), and say its sound as you write. Pupils should then try 
it two more times while you watch and provide feedback.
• Demonstrate writing the letter on the chalkboard once more.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter 5 times.

Baleemp,  Faan,  Kapiëts

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
• Read the following story aloud (use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if 
available)
• During reading, stop to discuss people and places
• Pause at 2-3 pictures throughout the book while reading. Ask pupils, based on the pictures, 
where they think the story takes place. Ask pupils, based on the pictures, what the characters 
like to do. Assure pupil responses are related to the pictures.
• Possible questions (use these, or ask your own questions):
• Where do you think they are? How do you know? What more can you say about that place?
• Who do you think this person is? What is he/she doing? 
• Talk about how the picture relates to parts of the story you are reading aloud.

JOMBIK NI BALEEMPUL
Uwal umpar wi, Jombik ci di kapiëts.
Unu ulon, a na win ne a fiër baleemp di kapiëtsul.
A na tsëp ee ñaan Ubob, "Elaan bi faan kii leemparin."
A ubob ja, "Uci Uguk dika bi, kee bi." Jombik ja, "Nin! Uguk dika bi." Jombik tsëp di Uguk a na ja wël, 
"Elaan bi faan kii leemparin."
Uguk jaul, "Uci Upíl kë bi, inji kam bi." Jombik ja,"Aa Nin! Upíl dika bi." Jombik tsëp di Upíl a na ja 
wël, "Elaan bi faan kii leemparin."
A Upíl jaul, "Uci Najan kë bi, inji kam bi." A Jombik ja wël,"Aa Nin! Najan dika bi." Jombik tsëp di 
Najan a na jaul, "Elaan bi faan kii leemparin."
Najan jaul, "Uci Ukopëtsats kë bi, inji kam bi." A Jombik jaul,"Aa Nin! Ukopëtsats dika bi." Jombik 
tsëp di Ukopëtsats a na wël, "Elaan bi faan kii leemparin."
Ukopëtsats jaul, "Uci Pëmúl kë bi, inji kam bi." A Jombik ja wël,"Aa Nin! Pëmúl dika bi." Jombik tsëp 
di Pëmúl a na pul, "Elaan bi faan kii leemparin."
Pëmúl jaul, "Uci Bërua kë bi, inji kam bi." A Jombik ja pul,"Aa Nin! Bërua dika bi." Jombik tsëp di 
Bërua a na bul, "Elaan bi faan kii leemparin."
Bërua jaul, "Uci Usubal kë sub, inji kam bi." A Jombik ja bul,"Aa Nin! Usubal dika sub." Unu këfa, a 
nga tsëp bëlieng kapiëts Jombik.
Uguk joont Ubob.
Upíl ruak Uguk ni ngëbúk wël. Najan tap Upíl.
Ukopëtsats rum Najan. Pëmúl fiŋ Ukopëtsats. Bërua tër Pëmúl.
Usubal jimb Bërua.
Din a Jombik tuk atsëp.

activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.

their own words. Ask pupils how the word was used in the story.
• Say: Ngëjej irim yi ngëjuk yi nja ka leemp-na ngëja ngëwalu.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil 
book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a 
new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the 
pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Review the question word "where"  "Tsum" •  
• Read the question:
• Tsum tsi Jombik cii-na tsun? (Jombik a cii-na di bëreeŋ bëwiak).
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Say: Tsum nda te përim pan pats pi pi ngëjej pi a yeparaan uyepar, pi ngëjuk pi tsi ngënu 
• Ngan par ngi?
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call on one or 
two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word "where" asks us about a place)
• Teach pupils to use the question word "when" (" Uwal/Lum")
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "when". Tell pupils that they will 
use it to answer the next question.
• Read the question: Uwal woom wi m ŋal wën puu noonts di utsand?
• Call on 2 pupils to answer. Their answer should be a time (i.e. in the morning, after school, on 
the weekend)
• Say: Uja utiis "Lum" (umpac wi: 'Lum')ka yeparaa-naa ngëyepar undo uwal. Man nja nte 'Lum' 
• ka me ne ujaankäma ka ci undo uwal. Apurir pëci uwal unu (kom, bëfa), unu kanëm (kom 
• Kaluund /Friday),oo uwal tsi uwaanu (kom pëti).

•  Read the question:
• Lum di Jombik ŋal run baleemp tsënkul di kapiëts?
• Answer: Jombik a ŋal baleemp tsënkul faan (unu ucints)
• Say: Ngëwejats ko wi ngëteen wi di kafëlal. Katëtan aja: "Nda bili faan ndii leemparin"
• Ask pupils to think about when, or the time, that this happened. 
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: Bi yën kuerar bukun upil pëngare? (Najan kuerarun upil 
• pëgare.)
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. 
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

• Ask pupils to think about the story, then think of something that these characters might like to 
eat.

2 examples for each character.
• Read the sentences back to pupils.

the character name in the sentence. If they are incorrect, try to help them recognize it. For 
example, point to the correct name at the top of the board, then ask them to try again.

Nuunu A Ŋal Iraala Iwalu
Nuunu ŋal pëka iraala iwalu. A na tsëp tsi bu këwaap-na tsi iraala.
Nawaap jaul, "Mbaandi tsi tsëko tsëmënts. Mán wëlu iraala iliingu yi." Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m 
ŋal ijankal?"
Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!" Nawaap yepar, "Tsum m ŋal ifëlal?" Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal iraala iruŋkëtuel?" Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal iraala indër yi utsia yul?" Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal iraala yi kan kul yi aa yuu tibar-a? Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal iraala yi kan yëk yi bërëm-a?" Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Din nawaap iraala cilan-ni utsand iraala icumal. Iraala gara a jëk tsëko tsëwaapi.
Tsi utuami, Nuunu win iraala yi na ŋal yi. Nuunu natsa a na tiëma yul.
Nawaap jaul, "O, Nuunu! Yi aci iraaloo ijon."

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud 
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available

Nuunu A Ŋal Iraala Iwalu
Nuunu ŋal pëka iraala iwalu. A na tsëp tsi bu këwaap-na tsi iraala. Nawaap jaul, "Mbaandi tsi tsëko 
tsëmënts. Mán wëlu iraala iliingu yi." Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal ijankal?"
Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!" Nawaap yepar, "Tsum m ŋal ifëlal?" Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal iraala iruŋkëtuel?" Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal iraala indër yi utsia yul?" Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal iraala yi kan kul yi aa yuu tibar-a? Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Nawaap yeparul, "Tsum m ŋal iraala yi kan yëk yi bërëm-a?" Nuunu yankësul, "Nin! Nin!"
Din nawaap iraala cilan-ni utsand iraala icumal. Iraala gara a jëk tsëko tsëwaapi.
Tsi utuami, Nuunu win iraala yi na ŋal yi. Nuunu natsa a na tiëma yul.
Nawaap jaul, "O, Nuunu! Yi aci iraaloo ijon."
Review the question word "where" ("Tsum   "), "who" ("Yën   ") and "when" ("Lum")
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call on one or 
two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word "where" asks us the name of someone or something alive)
• Read the question: 
• Tsum tsi Nuunu tsëp tsun kaweel iraala. ( Nuunu tsëp tsi tsëwaapi iraala).
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Continue by reviewing what each keyword is asking about, and then ask the question.
• Say: "Yën" ( kayepar inja pëjaankëmaan-na undo tsëko oo undo ko undolaa wi).
• Read the question: Yën ci wën tsi pëtsënk Nuunu pëtsas iraalaul iwalu? ( Ajug tsëwaapi iraala 
• ka tsënkun Nuunu pëtsas iraalaul iwalu).
• Say: "Lum" (Ka yepar inja pëjaankëmaan-na uwal oo unu).
• Read the question: Lum di Nuunu win dun iraala yi na ŋal yi?
• Answers may include:
• Bi iraala icumal garaa bi tsi pëkak,
• Bi nawaap iraala pënan-ni bi iraala icumal,

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "i" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Wi ci wën uwab inja uwalu par ntsari. Uwab wi aka bëruur /i/. Ngëja bëlieng: /i/.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "I " on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Wi a ci uwab uloole wën. Aka bëruur /I /. Uci ujuund-na uja oo katim, nja ka win wël iink.
• Point to the small letter "i" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ngëwal ngëcumal, ja ka win wël iink tsi irim.

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: We wi nda win wën?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help pupils 
understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Ngëwaaf iñan pëliingan ni itawar përim tsi /u/pi/. Ngëyaas um ngi nda te gun /i/ tsi 
• përim "upi "? Ngëwaaf kak.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the sound, 
help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another language 
they know.

• Say: Ngëja bëlieng përim pëcints pi. Përim pëcints aci " iru ". Tsum nda te bëruur /i/ tsi 
• përim "iru "? Ngyaas um ngi nda te gun bul?
• Say: Inkri aci uwal ind. Nda jaan përim. Uja ind, nda tsuun pëkuanj tsi utsia uwab /i/ uwal wi 
nda ru wi wël.
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Ind bëlieng nda tsuun pëkuanj tsi utsia pëfootu pëcäk di utsia. We wi nda win wën? Aci 
• "undiink".
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: Bëruur /i/ apurir buts pëyampanaa. Pacwën ne uci këja bul, këtiisan, pëtu bul bu yamp. 
• Tsum nda te bëruur uwab /ii/ tsi përim "undiink"?
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the same 
vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to each other. 
(Answer: two)
• Tell pupils that when they see two "i" together, it makes a long sound /ii/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long (stretched) 
sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the syllables 
and listen for the long vowel in the word

Reread the following story aloud

• Pause at 2-3 pictures throughout the book while reading. Ask pupils, based on the picture, 
where they think the story takes place. What time do they think it is? What do they think the

ABI NI UPI
Abi aci ni pëbukaul. Bu ka ngëkëmbe ngëtëb, ngëguk ngëwaants, uyët, ni upi. Upi aro ci ufuur. Ka 
jii-jian Abi undo ngëko bëfuur ngi-uu ro ngi.
Unu ulon, Abi win upi këro ko uwaraatsa wi. Ana tuk ee leents aninul. Maa aninul ro mi tsi uleemp. 
Ana jaul, "Oh Abi, wëtan bëleents." Na tuk ee leents tsëmakul niints. Maa tsëmakul niints mi tsi 
uleemp. Ana jaul, "Oh, Abi, wëtan bëleents."
A Abi tuk ee leents tsëmakul ŋaats. Maa na mi tsi uleemp. Ana jaul, "Oh, Abi, wëtan bëleents."
Tsi utuami, ana tuk ee leents atiëmul ŋaats. Atiëmul doots ci tsi përo ko. Ana jaul, "Abi, pëni kii 
piban-nin." Aba tukar tsi upi ci tsi. Upi aro ci tsi kare iŋi. A atiëmul lië, "Oh Nasien Batsi inji! Upi 
aci tsi kare-in iŋi!" Aninul tuki a nuu lië, "Iraala inji yuu-yun?" Asin nul tuki a nuu lië, " Ukalsa inji 
wël-wën?" Tsëmakul niints tuki a nuu lië, "Umanta inji wël-wën?" Tsëmakul ŋaats tuki a nuu lië, 
"Imiisa ikol inji yuu-yun?"
Aba teen bëlieng upi. A upi teen buts bukul a ukëkës. A atiëmul jej iŋiul ana buafats Abi. Ana 
ja,"Baran bi m leentin bi ko wi upi ro wi karo."

• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call on one or 
two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word "where" asks us about a place)
Teach pupils to use the question word  ("We ")
• Read the question:  "Mbuk mko moom mi m pemun pëŋal?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer.
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "what." Tell pupils that they will 
use it to answer the next question.
• Say: Përim "We" a leents inja par pëjej ko, oo uwejats par pëjaakëmaana. Man ja te "We" 
kame ne ujaakëma ka ci ko wi këwin wi te këkërara, oo ko umpats wi.
• Say: Uci win unjär utsooŋ a yepar, "We ci wën wi?" Man ŋal pëme katim wël. Uci yepar, 
• "We?"Man ŋal pëme ko wi ka njipanaana wi, ro wi.
• Read the question: We wi anin Abi ro wën ci tsi përo? (Anin Abi aro mi tsi kajant Mmaaj)
• Say: Ngëwejats ko wi ngëteen wi tsi kafëlal. Katëtan aja: Aninul aro mi ti uleemp oo aro kajant 
• Mmaaj."
• Ask pupils to think about what, or the thing, they are asking about. 
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: We wi upi këñaam wën? ( Upi kañaam iŋi)
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. Remind pupils that it is a "what" question.
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

learning_outcomes: Identify and say the target vowel sound, and recognize the letter that represents that sound.

activities.title: Letter review
activities.content:
Review small and capital letters
• Write the small letter "o" and capital letter "O" 
on the blackboard. 
• Ask pupils to raise their hands if they know the 
sound the letter makes. Call on a pupil to say it. 
Provide feedback.
• Ask pupils to find and point to the letter in their 
book. Ask the whole class to say the sound.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "o" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: "Wi ci wën uwab inja uwalu ntsari. Uwab wi aka bëruur /o/. Ngëja bëlieng: /o/."
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point: Wi a ci uwab uloole wën. Aka bëruur /O/. Uci ujuund- na uja oo katim, nja ka win wël 
iink /O/.
• Point to the capital letter "O" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Point to the small letter "o" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ngëwal ngëcumal, nja ka win wël iink tsi irim.

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: We wi nda win wën?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help pupils 
understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: Ngëwaaf iñan pëliingan ni bëruur tsi "kato". Ngëyaas um ngi nda te gun bëruur / o/ tsi 
• përim "kato"? Ngëwaaf bëruur kak.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the sound, 
help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another language 
they know.

• Say: Ngëja bëlieng përim pëcints pi:"ubopal". Tsum nda te bëruur / o/ tsi përim "ubopal"? 
• Ngyaas um ngi nda te gun bul?
• Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: "Ind bëlieng nda tsuun pëkuanj tsi utsia pëfootu pëcäk di utsia. We wi nda win wën? Aci " 
uloong".
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: Bëruur /o/ apurir buts pëyampanaan. Pac wën ne uci këja bul, këtiisan, pëtsu bul bu 
yamp. Tsum nda te bëruur uwab /oo/ tsi përim "uloong "?
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the same 
vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to each other. 
Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two "o" together, it makes a long sound /oo/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long (stretched) 
sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the syllables 
and listen for the long vowel in the word.

learning_outcomes: Use illustrations while reading.
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Use verbal and nonverbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: How to read – using illustrations
activities.content:
Teach how to think about illustrations while reading
• Say: "Pëteen ifootu ka tsënk inja par pëme uwar 
ko wi katëtan ja wi,ko wi ka pac wi, tsi ka roon-na 
tsi,ni uwal wi urolaa wi. Ntsari, man teen kafëlal ka 
leents ind katëtan. Uteen inji katëtan, nja këjeenj, 
nja ka ñakanaan undo ifootu impats yi."
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
Uleemp, Bëleents, Atuk

activities.title: Read aloud (Big Book)
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud 
• See the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available)
• During reading, stop to discuss people and things in the story.
• Pause at 2-3 pictures throughout the book while reading. Ask pupils, based on the picture, 
who they think the character(s) is/are. Also ask questions that use the word "what." Assure 
pupil responses are related to the picture.
• Possible questions (use these, or ask your own questions):
• Who is going to the _____?
• What is this thing? What kind of thing (for example, animal, house, etc.) is this? 
• Talk a bit about how the picture relates to parts of the story you are reading aloud.

SUSAN BONATSÄTS
Mama ja, "Uwal kare uwai aband." Maa Susan bonatsäts.
Papa jaul, "Susan,pëni këreala! Aci përe pi mŋal pi."Maa Susan bonatsäts.
Mama yaa-rul kaya ki përe pi Susan pepi pëŋal, un ci wi bëtër umaani ni ngëtsëb. Maa Susan 
bonatsäts.
Papa wupul. Maa Susan bonatsäts.
Mama wëlul përe tsi pëkanda. Maa Susan bonatsäts.
 Papa cielarul pëmangu. Maa Susan bonatsäts.
 Mama ja, "Uwal aband m doon këreala."
Susan ja, "Mama, m fin ne m wëlin ba uwai?"

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils at random to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning 
in their own words.
• Say: Ngëjej irim inja iwalu ngëleemp-na ngëja.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil 
book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a 
new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the 
pupils, depending on the responses

activities.content:

learned.
• Pupils say the sounds of the letters.

activities.title: Teach pupils to hear syllables
activities.content:
Clap words with different numbers of syllables
• Say: "Tsi ujuundi bëjuk, tsi uwal bëjuk inja, ngëjuk ne ngëyilan pëpatsës irim nja ka tsu yul tsi 
itawar. Katawar kan ci ki, aka bëruur kul. Mán wël ind ngënaamanaani ngëtëb. Nda teenan 
uwar. Ngëwaaf iñan nja ka teen."
• Model by clapping syllables. Read the word once, then clap the syllables:  a/cii/na/ "aciina"
• Practice together with pupils. Read the word once, then clap the syllables with pupils.  
      u/ŋiil// (uŋiil)
• Pupils practice alone. Read the word once, then ask pupils to clap the syllables independently 
(without the teacher). Pëfiitu: pë-fii-tu, Miiraan: mii-raan, Liincani: liin-ca-ni)
• Give pupils feedback words they have difficulty with. Help them hear the syllable breaks.

activities.title: Pre-activity vocabulary
activities.content:
Discuss pictures
• Have pupils point to the first picture in the Pupil Book,  " ." Ask them what they think it is. 
Ask them what they know about it, or their experiences. (For example, "Have you seen this/it 
before?" "Where?" "What is it like?").
• Discuss each picture for 1 minute or less until the end of the page.
Pictures
• ilaak
• pëleele

• pëlok
• uloong
• undiink
• ubob
Hear and see the vowel within a word
• Say: Nda yueran pëkuanj tsi pëfootu pan ci pi di ngëbuk ind. We win da win wën? (Confirm 
that what they say matches the word in the book, or correct it).
• Ask pupils to clap the syllables in the word once.
• Say: Ngëja, nja ka waaf iñan, pëliingan ni bëruur ban ci bi. Bëruur aci/u/. Inkri nda tsuun 
• pëkuanj tsi bëruur /uu/ bëtsiisan tsi përim uloong. 
• Demonstrate in a pupil book by touching the first picture and the vowels that match the 
picture. Walk around the room so pupils can see your finger on the correct picture and vowels.
• Ask pupils to repeat with the next picture. Clap the word with them. Then ask the pupils what 
vowel sounds they heard. Repeat, or say, the correct answer for the whole class to hear. Then 
ask the class to touch the picture and the vowels.
• Once pupils are comfortable with this, clap each word with them. After each word, ask them to 
find the matching vowels by themselves. 
• Check their work as they go.

activities.title: Sight word review
activities.content:
Review the sight words through shared writing
• Say: Nda jun ngëjuk kak undo ngëko ngëtëb nga pats ngi, ngi ngëro gi juk.
• Write the two sight words (Upa, Abi) on the top of the board.
• Ask pupils to think of a place that these characters might like to go.
• Call on 3-4 pupils at random to give you some ideas. Guide pupils to choose a character name, 
and say where they might like to go. Write the sentences on the board. For example, (Abi a ŋal 
• kaya babuëts di bërëk) Try to get at least 2 examples for each character.
• Read the sentences back to pupils.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "We  "
• Read the question: 
• We wi nda ŋal wën përo uci nda wëtan ikol?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer.
• Say: Ngëro juk bi përim "We" leents inja bi par pëjej katim ko pëjaankëmaa-na uyepar.
• Say: Ucints kak wi përim "We" këyepar wi, ka ci undo uwejats iñaan ni bi na win bi ko. Uci 
• yepar, "We wi Susan këwejats wën?" Man ŋal ind pëleents in ko wi nda wejats wi ne Susan aci 
• ri pëwejats. Ngëjaankëma uyepar wan. Nda jun ngëjaankëma kak ngëyepar "We".
Read the question:
• What did Adama's father do to carry her so she would eat?
• We wi asin Susan këro wën pur pëjaul na reala"( Asin Susan aja naroon nu wupul).
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: We wi anin Susan fin wën? ( Anin Susan aro fin ne nako ro wëlul ba uway.)
• Call on pupils at random to respond.

activities.content:
Special assessment - Assess Week 2 vowels: say the 
letter sound 
• Write the two vowels learned this week on the 
board lesson
• Say: "Man ŋal pëtsu kañan inji tsi utsia uwab ucäk. 
• Uci baandi di wi,man ŋal m doon këkuetanin bëruur 
wël di kabats.
• Walk around, and listen to 5 pupils tell you the sound. If they don't all say the correct sound, 
tell pupils the sound, and then repeat. Do this up to 2 times.

• Tell pupils you will say words with short and long vowels. Ask pupils to raise their hands.

• Say: Ind bëlieng nda tsuun pëkuanj tsi utsia pëfootu pëcäk. We wi nda win wën? Aci " .

what picture and letters they are touching.
• Continue to clap the words under each picture with them. After each word, ask them to find 
the matching vowels independently. Check their work as they go.
• Continue until both pages in the Pupil Book are done.

activities.content:
• Say: " Inkri mán ja uruur. Uci nda te wël, nda tsuun pëkuanj di utsia uwab unka wi bëruur bi.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Identify and say the target sound, and recognize the letter that represents that sound.
Blend letter sounds to read syllables and syllables to read words.
Read syllables quickly and accurately.

activities.title: Rapid letter review
activities.content:
Review small and capital letters
• Review small and capital letters.

activities.title: Teach the sound
activities.content:
Tongue twister-say the sound
• Say the tongue twister. Pupils repeat
Baaba ba ebe Aba
• Ask pupils what sound they hear most. Answer: /b../
Listening game - first sound 
• Say each word below. Pupils put a hand up if they hear the /b/ sound at the beginning of the 
word and on the desk if they do not.
Baaba win ebe Buba ba aci

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small "b " on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: " Wi ci wën uwab inja uwalu ntsari. Aka bëruur /b/  
• Say: Ngëja bëlieng /b/.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter " B" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: "Wi aci uwab uloole wën, ngëko naam bëruur /B/. Uci ukurna uja, ni katim, iink ri ja këwin 
dun wël."
• Point to the small letter "b " on the alphabet poster or on the board again.

• Say: "Ngëwal ngëcumal iink di nja kë win ndun ngul tsi irim"
Keyword picture study
• Say: We wi nda win wën?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: Ngëja përim pi /Baaba/. Tsum nda te bëruur uwab/b/ tsi përim "Baaba"?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Përim pënjämp aci /Baaba/.
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of 
the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "aa" and show the  "b "
• Say: Uwab wi aka bëruur boom? (pupils respond "b".)
• Cover the " b" and show the "aa."
• Say: Uwab wi aka bëruur boom? "aa"
• Say: "Nda yil puu teen bëruur ndu pats bul, uba ndu bofëlän bul karo katawar përim. Inkri 
• nda ruun ngul nda bofëlän /b /aa/ "baa"
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: "Nda cëkëndäni uwar ndu teen. Mán teen itawar përim ka bofëlän yul karo përim".
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: Ngëteen ko wi bëlieng. 
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try reading the 
same word by themselves. 
• Say: Inkri nda me ko wi nda ka wi përo. NJa ka teen irim ilon di ngëbuk ind. NJa ka juund-na 
pëteen 
• itawar përim uba nja ka ja irim. Nda tsuun pëkuanj pëfetsanaan. : (Monitor and help pupils.)

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of new and previously learned letters to read a short text independently.
Make predictions using a picture.
Write a new letter.

activities.title: My language
activities.content:
Teach a rule of the language
• Help pupils to find my language picture box in the 
Pupil's Book. 
• Say: Aja nja këja oo nja këcikëndän irim oo ngëja 
balon tsi pëleents inja, aka ngëlay ngi ngëka ngi 
pëfets. Ngëlay ngi ka tsënk inja ngun pëme uwar 
ko wi bu këja wi oo ko wi nja këja wi. Ntsari, 
ngëcikëndän ulon tsi ngëlay ngi. 
• Say: We wi nda win wën tsi pëfootu pi?
• Say: Inkri nda cikëndäni uwar. Mán ja përim oo uja.
      Pëboola inji
      Kamaañ inji
• Say: We wi nda me wën tsi përim pi oo uja wi? Apac we?
• Uci m win upicanaa kom "Pëboola inji," a pac ne inji ka un pëboola.
• Say: Uja woom oo përim poom piban pun ko wi nda win wi di pëfootu?
• Call 1-2 learners to give similar example of my language rule and explain what it means. Focus 
on my language examples in pupils' examples.

activities.title: Vocabulary – Before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Write the vocabulary on the board (but not the definitions). Ask pupils what they know about 
each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know. 
aba      abi

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction
activities.content:
Prediction based on picture
• Help pupils find the decodable text of the day in their Pupil Books by holding up the page and 
saying the page number.
• Say: "Nda teenan pëfootu pi. We wi nda win wën? We wi nda wejats wën ne keerolaa tsi 
• katëtan?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then invite them to share their predictions with a partner. Call 
on 2 pupils at random and ask for their predictions.

activities.title: Reason to read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Unu ulon, anin Baaba ni Aba juŋ përe pëlilal. Ana yis bukul abofëlän ana jukan di untabël. 
Baaba bi baandi ucäk ana re piicul. Aro ŋal përe pi Aba. 
• Ngëteen tsi katëtan nja ka me përe pi anin bukul juŋ pi, ni buts ne Baaba bi re ank përe Aba.
• Say: Nda Jejan umeind wi nda ka wi tsi ngëwab ni itawar përim, ndu leents-na katëtan ki
• bërierind. Uci nduu teen kafëlal, ndu tsu pëkuanj kafetsanaan irim.

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. Do NOT read it aloud for them. They 
should whisper read (read quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If 
pupils finish reading early, they can read the story again with a partner.

activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment.

Then make 3 more columns with the title "letters",

activities.title: Reason to Read

Think about why you want to read the story
Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual pupils.
• Say: Napats nampëli ni ndëpaas aci tsi përoolär ngëko pëji te kaats na mee I ko wi acints ci wi 
tsi përo. Ngëteen tsi katëtan nja kame ko wi ba tuamanaan win ni ko wi ba ro wi ci tsi përo.
• Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list.
• Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. 
• This gives a general sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 
1-5 may indicate that the child is struggling. 

• Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
• Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".               
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?

• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: We wi përim pi pac wën?

FAATU NI PËLI
Faatu aci napëli ni kalilan ni uwal un ci wi.
Aja na roon nuu noonts ni ngëjär ngan ci ngi, ito mko, ilaak,upats, bakaats, ni ko wi na win wi ba rin di 
bëreeŋ. Maa ko wi nape wi pëŋal pënoontsna, aci pëli. Aja na roon nu ŋal pëmob pul, maa tsënkanäts.
Ana paya bëko bayamp bi mak, ne kañnul kee tsënkan-ank pëli, maa kañanul tsënkanäts. Ana jukan usieu 
mlik alawan, koo teen ulimts pëli.
Ana niaj uniëul a katse win pëli! Din ana teen tsi kateenaraan-ni, ana win pëlon pëli! Maa na me ne pëli 
aci pëloole rin.
Maa bi pëli yabi-aa pakaki, ana pikëra. Ana rug di bëkaabul te asinul te. Asinul bi ri pëfërul. Asinul 
yeparul, "Faatu inji, we wi kërug wën?" Ana jaul, "Itsënkanäts pëli!"
Asinul jaul, "M di këyilan ka mob pëli. Wi m yilan wi përo ci wën pëmob ulimts pul."
Faatu wejats ne aka ngëlimts ngëcumal, te upats bacumal kee yil pënoonts-na ngul. Maa pëli pi, iñaan di 
ka yilan pëmob pul, aci pëloole rin.
Ana ja,"Ko wi awara. Apiban ne, pëli aci pi bañaan bëlieng."

FAATU NI PËLI
Faatu aci napëli ni kalilan ni uwal un ci wi.
Aja na roon nuu noonts ni ngëjär ngan ci ngi, ito mko, ilaak,upats, bakaats, ni ko wi na win wi ba 
rin di bëreeŋ. Maa ko wi nape wi pëŋal pënoontsna, aci pëli. Aja na roon nu ŋal pëmob pul, maa 
tsënkanäts.
Ana paya bëko bayamp bi mak, ne kañnul kee tsënkan-ank pëli, maa kañanul tsënkanäts. Ana jukan 
usieu mlik alawan, koo teen ulimts pëli.
Ana niaj uniëul a katse win pëli! Din ana teen tsi kateenaraan-ni, ana win pëlon pëli! Maa na me ne 
pëli aci pëloole rin.
Maa bi pëli yabi-aa pakaki, ana pikëra. Ana rug di bëkaabul te asinul te. Asinul bi ri pëfërul. Asinul 
yeparul, "Faatu inji, we wi kërug wën?" Ana jaul, "Itsënkanäts pëli!"
Asinul jaul, "M di këyilan ka mob pëli. Wi m yilan wi përo ci wën pëmob ulimts pul."
Faatu wejats ne aka ngëlimts ngëcumal, te upats bacumal kee yil pënoonts-na ngul. Maa pëli pi, 
iñaan di ka yilan pëmob pul, aci pëloole rin.
Ana ja,"Ko wi awara. Apiban ne, pëli aci pi bañaan bëlieng."

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list.
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 

that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE 
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".

Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
•  Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
•  Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
•  Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: We wi përim pi pac wën?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: "Mán ci tsi pëwejats përim. Përim pi aci "beka ". Nda cikëndäni uwar ndu waaf bëruur 
• ban ci bi tsul /be/ ka/.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the page in their Pupil Books. Then, 
write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.

• Say: "Përim aci "beka '. Inkri ngëpican përim pi. Ngëja pul bëlieng". (Pupils read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their 
copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the rest 
of the words. Words /be/ /ka/ "beka"; /ka/ ki/ "kaki"; /a/ /bek/ "abek"; /a/ / be/ /ka/ 
" abeka"; 
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: "Inkri ma ŋal nda teen ne nduu yilank pëjej itawar përim nda leemp-na irim".
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a partner to share the word they made

activities.title: Letter and keyword: p ; paapa
activities.content:
Teach the letter  p
•  Point to the small letter "p" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Wi ci wën uwab inja uwalu ntsari. Uwab wi aka bëruur /p/. Ngëja bëlieng /p/. 
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).

• Say: Uwab wi aci uloole wën. Aka buts bëruur /P/. Nja ka win unaam iink uci uci tsi ujuundi 
uja, oo tsi katim.
• Point to the small letter "p" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ngëwal ngëcumal tsi irim, nja ka win unaam iink. 
Keyword picture study

•  Say: We wi nda win wën?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: Ngëja përim pi: "paapa". Tsum nda te bëruur /p/ tsi përim,"paapa"?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)

• Say: We wi përim pi pac wën?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.
3. Word building (10mins)
Use syllables to build given words
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board.
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "aa" and show the "p". 
• Say: We ci wën bëruur bi? (pupils respond "p")
• Cover the "p" and show the "aa".
• Say: We ci wën bëruur bi? (pupils respond "aa").
• Say: Ngëteen bëruur bëlieng nja ka bofëlän ka ro katawar përim. Inkri ngëja bëruur /p/aa, 
"paa".
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

3. Read Word (10mins)

Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Nda cikëndäni ndu teen.Mán teen tsi kafëlal itawar përim yi, uba kabofëlän yul ka ro 
përim.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: Ngëja bëling.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
the same word by themselves.
• Say: Inkri nda me ko wi nda ka wi përo. Nda teenan irim icints di ngëbuk 
• ind. Ucäk, nda teenan itawar përim, ndu ru përim. Nda fetsani ni pëkuanj. (Monitor and help 
pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

UBÚK UKOPËTSATS
Unu ulon, ubúk ukopëtsats pëni di pëkueb pëtiis. Uteen ngëbúúru bëlieng a u win 
ukac. Ukac ja wël, "Ubúk ukopëtsats, m pats bënaam." A u yepar ukac, "We ka wën?" 
Ukac ja wël, "Parme m kaats ibaakëla."Ubúk ukopëtsats juatsän a upën atsëp.
Jonats a u tsënk umbëkëmbëk. Umbëkëmbëk ja wël, "Ubúk ukopëtsats, m pats bënaam." 
A u yepar wël, "We ka wën?" Umbëkëmbëk ja wël, "Parme m yilats pëyits."
Ubúk ukopëtsats ci tsi bëga wël a wii tsënk ubopal. Ubopal ja wël, "Ubúk ukopëtsats, 
m pats bënaam." Ubúk ukopëtsats yepar wël, "We ka wën?" Ubopal ja wël, "Parme m 
kaats itsiim, te m yilats pëcat."Ubúk ukopëtsats rug, a u ja, "O,nin! Ulon ucär man 
pats bënaam."
Din ubúk ukopëtsats tsënk upil. Upil yepar wël, "M ci yën?" Ubúk ukopëtsats ja wël, 
"I meets." Upil ja wël, "Tsiisan kii tsënk aninu." Uunk, ubúk ukopëtsats tsiis. Uband 
wël, a u win ukopëtsats ujinal uyampal, wi kan kúl wi. A unin wël ja wël, "Abúk inji! 
M do ya tsum?"
Ubúk ukopëtsats muëj pëji. Inkri a u me uwar: Uko patsats bënaam. "Man ci ukopëtsatste ko wi rin, a liing."

activities.title: Comprehension – Factual & inferential questions
activities.content:
Ask factual questions

• Question: [ANSWER: Please check from sentence 3]
• 1. Upi Upa a ka we? Ujaankëma: Upi Upa aka upi.
• 2. We wi Upa do wën Paapa? Ujaankëma: Upa a bek Paapa upi ka upi].
• After the response, congratulate, help, or correct the pupil's answer. If the pupil is partly 
correct or incorrect, tell them why. Help pupils find the sentence in the story that contains the 
answer.
Ask inferential questions
• Say: Mán yepar ind ngëyepar ngi ka tsu ind ngi ndu wejats kapatslän. Ngërika win ujaankëma u 
mab wi tsi katëtan. Maa nja ka leemp-na katëtan ni ume wi ngëka wi par pëjaankëma ngëyepar 
ngi.

• Question 1: Tsum tsi Maama kaanitsun ucam?Ujaankëma: Maama aweeli ucam di kanëm.

• After each question, call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss 
their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about what is in the text or picture, as well 

as their own experiences, to reflect on what may have given them that idea.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "p" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Wi ci wën uwab inja uwalu ntsari. Uwab wi aka bëruur /p/. Ngëja bëlieng /p/. 
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the small letter "p" on the alphabet poster or on the board again. • Say: Ngëwal 
ngëcumal tsi irim, nja ka win wël unaam iink /p/.
Keyword picture study
• Say: We wi nda win wën?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: Ngëja përim pi: "Paapa". Tsum nda te bëruur /p/ tsi përim,"Paapa"?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Përim pënjämp aci: "Paapa."
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of 
the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board.
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "aa" and show the "p". 
• Say: Bëruur bi aci boom? (pupils respond "p") 
• Cover the "p" and show the "aa".
• Say: Bëruur bi aci boom? (pupils respond /aa/)
• Say: Ngëteen bëruur bëlieng nja ka bofëlän yul ka ro katawar përim. Inkri, ngëja bëruur /paa/, 
"paa".
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words

Blending syllables to read words

• Say: Nda cikëndäni ndu teen.Mán teen tsi kafëlal itawar përim yi, uba kabofëlän yul ka ro 
përim.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: Nda jun ngëteen wël bëlieng.
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
the same word by themselves.
• Say: A (Monitor and help pupils).
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

UBÚK UKOPËTSATS
Unu ulon, ubúk ukopëtsats pëni di pëkueb pëtiis. Uteen ngëbúúru bëlieng a u win ukac. Ukac ja wël, 
"Ubúk ukopëtsats, m pats bënaam." A u yepar ukac, "We ka wën?" Ukac ja wël, "Parme m kaats 
ibaakëla."Ubúk ukopëtsats juatsän a upën atsëp.
Jonats a u tsënk umbëkëmbëk. Umbëkëmbëk ja wël, "Ubúk ukopëtsats, m pats bënaam." A u yepar 
wël, "We ka wën?" Umbëkëmbëk ja wël, "Parme m yilats pëyits."
Ubúk ukopëtsats ci tsi bëga wël a wii tsënk ubopal. Ubopal ja wël, "Ubúk ukopëtsats, m pats 
bënaam." Ubúk ukopëtsats yepar wël, "We ka wën?" Ubopal ja wël, "Parme m kaats itsiim, te m 
yilats pëcat."Ubúk ukopëtsats rug, a u ja, "O,nin! Ulon ucär man pats bënaam."
Din ubúk ukopëtsats tsënk upil. Upil yepar wël, "M ci yën?" Ubúk ukopëtsats ja wël, "I meets." Upil 
ja wël, "Tsiisan kii tsënk aninu." Uunk, ubúk ukopëtsats tsiis. Uband wël, a u win ukopëtsats ujinal 
uyampal, wi kan kúl wi. A unin wël ja wël, "Abúk inji! M do ya tsum?"
Ubúk ukopëtsats muëj pëji. Inkri a u me uwar: Uko patsats bënaam. "Man ci ukopëtsats-te ko wi 
rin, a liing."

activities.title: Assessment: BEFORE THE LESSON
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment.
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. List 
all the pupils in the class in alphabetical order. 
Then make 3 more columns with the title "letters", 
"syllables" and "individual score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find the 
decodable story for this lesson. Instruct pupils who 
are not being assessed to read the story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: Upa ni Paapa bu ro ci tsi mantotëlär ni kampe yi acints. Ngëteen tsi katëtan ko wi 
• ba ro wi ka ro.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.
