activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have 
learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. 
• Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their 
words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: Përim pi a pac we?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.
3. Word building (10 mins)
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Mán ci tsi pëwejats përim. Përim pi aci "/u/ /paab/". Nda jun ngëwaaf itawar pul.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: Përim pi aci "/upaab/". Inkri ngëpican itawar përim kabofëlän. Nda jun ngëjapul bëlieng. 
(Pupils read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their 
copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the rest 
of the words.
• Words: /u/ paab/ "upaab" /ka/ /paab/ "kapaab" /u/ /pi/  "upi" 
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Inkri, man ŋal nda roon ndu teen pëleemp irim-ind bërierind.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.

vocabulary word the pupils just learned or when you hear a syllable the pupils just practiced.
JUKIN NI MARIE
Unu ulon, Jukin bitse car a natsee. Asinul Paapa Pol, jaul,"Jukin m dikëya ikol ntsari-a?' A Jukin 
jaankëma ul, 'Wënd a ric bëga.' Jukin tuk a tsëp tsi ngëpi ni ngëkarnel ci tsi. A na tukar mjeenj 
ee jeji. Marie a ci atsaul ŋaats. Na tsëp pëtsënk Jukin pëwël ngënjär bareala. Marie wël ngëguk 
kacupan. Jukin wël ngëpi ni ngëkarnel pëtsats. A ngënjär kur pëleents ni ulilan. Marie lilan. A na ja, 
'Ngënjär alilan mak!' Marie yepar Jukin, 'Uci ngëwëlats ngënjär ngi bareala, we ka ro wën ngul ?' A 
Jukin jaul, 'Ngëko ka cats. Ngëbira ngul aci tsi iñan inja pur pëteen ngul uwar. Ngëko ci ngënjär ito.' 
Jukin ja, 'Uci nga ro ci ngënjär bëreeŋ kom ngëloong ni ngëbaca, ngu teen iyeen ngul.' Maa ngëpi 
inja ni ngëkarnel, ni ngëguk, ka atsaraan inja pëwël ngul bareala, mlik, ni tsëko tsi nguu ci tsi."
Anin bukul bi tsi bukul a na ja bukul, "Nda mob ngënjär ngi ni kañan kawar, ngëko lilan, a nja buts 
ngëlilan.''

JUKIN NI MARIE
Unu ulon, Jukin bitse car a natsee. Asinul Paapa Pol, jaul,"Jukin m dikëya ikol ntsari-a?' A Jukin 
jaankëma ul, 'Wënd a ric bëga.' Jukin tuk a tsëp tsi ngëpi ni ngëkarnel ci tsi. A na tukar mjeenj 
ee jeji. Marie a ci atsaul ŋaats. Na tsëp pëtsënk Jukin pëwël ngënjär bareala. Marie wël ngëguk 
kacupan. Jukin wël ngëpi ni ngëkarnel pëtsats. A ngënjär kur pëleents ni ulilan. Marie lilan. A na ja, 
'Ngënjär alilan mak!' Marie yepar Jukin, 'Uci ngëwëlats ngënjär ngi bareala, we ka ro wën ngul ?' A 
Jukin jaul, 'Ngëko ka cats. Ngëbira ngul aci tsi iñan inja pur pëteen ngul uwar. Ngëko ci ngënjär ito.' 
Jukin ja, 'Uci nga ro ci ngënjär bëreeŋ kom ngëloong ni ngëbaca, ngu teen iyeen ngul.' Maa ngëpi 
inja ni ngëkarnel, ni ngëguk, ka atsaraan inja pëwël ngul bareala, mlik, ni tsëko tsi nguu ci tsi."
Anin bukul bi tsi bukul a na ja bukul, "Nda mob ngënjär ngi ni kañan kawar, ngëko lilan, a nja buts 
ngëlilan.''

activities.title: Comprehension – Factual & inferential questions
activities.content:
Ask factual questions

• After the response, congratulate, help, or correct the pupil's answer. If the pupil is partly 
correct or incorrect, tell them why. Help pupils find the sentence in the story that contains the 
answer.
Ask inferential questions
• Ask each of the following questions.
• Question 1: We ka wën Paapa Pol yepar Jukin ne di kaya ikol ? Parme Paapa Pol a ŋal pëwëlul 
uleemp.
• Question 2: We ka wën a anin bi Jukin lilan? [Alilan parme ngär a dëmb/aka uliaf.] 
• After each question, pupils talk in pairs about their answers. Call on a pupil randomly to share 
their answer to the question. Discuss their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about 
what is in the text or picture, as well as their own experiences, to reflect on what may have 
given them that idea.

activities.title: Assessment: BEFORE THE LESSON
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the title 
"letters", "syllables" and "individual score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find 
the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct 
pupils who are not being assessed to read the 
story quietly..

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: Pënak unu Kainjan (Saturday) pëlon, upats batëb tseenda ko maa bu meets. Ngëteen di 
katëtan nja ka me bi bee me ko wi. 
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 

that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have 
learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to 
say the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter 
sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share 
their words, then move on to the next letter.

 Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: Përim pi pac we?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Mán ci tsi pëwejats përim. Përim pi aci "/kabëb/". Nda jun ngëteen nja ka waaf itawar 
pul.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: Përim pi aci "/kabëb/". Inkri ngëpican përim bëlieng.Nda jun ngëja pul bëlieng uyaas 
uloole. 
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their 
copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the rest 

of the words.
Words: : /ka/ bëb/, /pë/ kaba/, /bë/ kaab/,/u/këb/..
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Inkri, man ŋal nda roon ndu teen pëleemp irim-ind bërierind.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "c" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Wi ci wën uwab inja uwalu ntsari. Aka bëruur /c/. Ngëja bëlieng /c/. 
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "C" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: "Wi aci uwab uloole wën. Aka buts bëruur /C/. Uci uci ucäk tsi ujuundi uja, oo tsi katim, 
nja ka win wël iink"
• Point to the small letter "c" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.

Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: "Përim aci "cok".
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of 
the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board.
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "o" and show the "c". 
• Say: Bëruur boom bi (pupils respond /c/)
• Cover the "c" and show the "o".
• Say "Bëruur boom bi  (pupils respond "o")
• Say: Nda jun ngëja bëruur bëlieng, nja ka bufëlän ngul kaja katawar përim. Inkri, nda jaan 
bëruur. Nda yil pëja bëruur nda patsës uba ndu bofëlän yul ka ro katawar përim. Nda jaan 
bëruur bëlieng ndu bofëlän yul kak ka ro katawar përim./c/o/ "co".
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Nda cikëndäni uwar ndu teen. Mán nja itawar përim uba ka bofëlän yul ka ro përim.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: "Ngëteen ne ko wi."
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
the same word by themselves.
• Say Say Inkri nda me ko wi nda ka wi përo. Nda teenan irim icints di ngëbuk ind. Ucäk, nda 
teenan itawar përim, ndu ru përim. Nda tsuun pëkuanj nda fetsanaan. (Monitor and help 
pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

Think about why you want to read the story

Pupils read aloud in the book independently

should whisper read (read quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If 
pupils finish reading early, they can read the story again with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they have learnt to 
read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables to read words.

Check prediction based on picture

moment to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were what happened in the 
story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. Ask the 
pupils if those predictions were what happened.

Pupils practice writing the letter

to share the words they found.
• Write the letter "c" on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as you do it. 
Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of the letter. 
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "c" 5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins with the sound 
/c/.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud
• Ask pupils to do a thumbs up if they hear one of the new vocabulary words during the read 
aloud.
• Show the picture that goes with the story as you read aloud. Or, if you have the NALAP big 
book, use that to show the pictures.
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments such 
as when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learnt or when you hear a syllable the 
pupils just practiced.
UKAC UNTEERU NI UJUGËRI
Ukac Unteeru ni Ujugëri aci ifetsar. A nga ciina di bëko bëyampal.
Unu ulon Ukac Unteeru ja,"Ngëleemp bëcang." Maa Ujugëri ja, "Faan jakee leemp bëcang."
Unu utëbantsän, Ukac Unteeru ja, "Ngëleemp bëcang." Maa Ujugëri ja, "Faan jakee leemp bëcang."
Unu uwaajatsän, Ukac Unteeru ja, "Ngëleemp bëcang." Maa Ujugëri ja, "Faan jakee leemp bëcang."
Din, Ukac Unteeru leemp bëcang wël.
Maa Ujugëri ja ,"Faan meen leemp bëcang inji."
Unu ulon, bënu yëk mak tsi ngëkac. Ukac Unteeru yits ee niaj bëcang wël. Maa Ujugëri kaats bëcang.
Unu këfa, ufuts futs, a ufuts mak. Ukac Unteeru yits ee niaj bëcang wël kak. Maa Ujugëri kaats 
bëcang te inkri. Ufa unu kak, usubal sub, a usub mak. Ukac Unteeru yits ee niaj bëcang wël. Maa 
Ujugëri te inkri kaats bëcang.
Uunk bënu tër Ujugëri ufuts futs Ujugëri, A usubal subar Ujugëri. Maa unu un ci wi Ujugëri këja, 
"Faan mee leemp bëcang."

• Say: "Ngëjej irim yi ngëjuk yi ngëleemp na ngëja ngëwalu."

pupil book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a 
new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the 
pupils, depending on the responses.
• Remind pupils that they can use these words anytime throughout the day. Encourage pupils to 
share the words with their families at home.

challenging words.
• Walk around the room while pupils read. Encourage pupils to use skills they have learnt to 
read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables to read words..

Question 1: We wi Ciici ka wën?  [Ujaankëma: Ciici a ka ukac]
Question 2:  We wi Abi ro wën ukac Ciici?  [Unjaankëma: Abi a win ukac Ciici]
Which part of the story makes you think so?"
• After each question, call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss 
their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about what is in the text or picture, as well 
as their own experiences, to reflect on what may have given them that idea.
Make text-to-self connections
• Say: Aja ngëteen katëtan tsi kafëlal, kako ka lesan inja ngëko nga par ngi tsi ngëbira inja.
• Say: Inkri, nda wejatsi ko wi, uci m pën pëya tsëko a m bi m niaman ko, um di këci run?
• Ask pupils to turn to a partner to share their answers.
• Call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss their answer with the 
class. Help the pupils think about how the story relates to their own lives and how they can 
use their own experiences to understand the story.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "c" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Wi ci wën uwab inja uwalu ntsari. Uwab wi a ka bëruur /c/. Ngëja bëlieng /c/.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "C" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say:"Wi aci uwab uloole wën. A ka buts bëruur /C/. Uci uci ucak tsi ujuundi uja, oo tsi katim, 
ja ka win iink wël "
• Point to the small letter "c" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ngëwal ngëcumal tsi irim, ja ka win wël unaam iink /c/.

Keyword picture study
• Say: We wi nda win wën?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: Ngëja përim pi: "cok". Tsum nda te bëruur /c/ tsi përim,"cok"?
•  Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: Përim aci "cok"
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of 
the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board.
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "o" and show the "c"
•  Say: Bëruur boom bi?  (pupils respond "c")
• Cover the "c" and show the "o".
• Say: Bëruur bi aci boom? (pupils respond "o").
• Say: "Ngëteen bëruur bëlieng ja ka bofëlän bul karo katawar përim. Inkri, ngëja bëruur kak 
uloole, uloole /c/,/o/ " co".
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable.
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Nda cikëdäni ndu teen. Mán teen tsi kafëlal itawar përim, uba kabofëlän yul karo përim.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: "Nda jun ngëteen ne wël bëlieng"..
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 

the same word by themselves.
• Say: : "Inkri, nda me ko wi nda ka wi përo. Nda teenan ngëpic ngëcints ngun tsi ngëbuk ind. 
Ucäk, nda teenan itawar përim uba ind, ndu ja përim. Nda tsuun pëkuanj ndu fetsanaan. 
(Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

ngi pëfets. Ngëlay ngi ka tsënk inja ngun pëme 
uwar ko wi bu këja wi oo ko wi ja këja wi. Ntsari, 
ngëcikëndän ulon tsi ngëlay ngi. 
• Say: We wi nda win wën tsi pëfootu pi?
• Say: Inkri nda cikëndäni uwar. Mán ja përim oo uja. 
• Kee tana
• A tsef 
• Say: We wi nda me wën tsi përim pi oo uja wi? Apac we? 
• Uci upicanaa "A"tsi karo ko, apac ne ko umënts arolaa ba. Kom "Atana", "Atsef". Maa uci 
• upicanaa 'Kee" tsi karo ko, apac ne ko umënts netse rolaa, kom "Keetana," "Keetsef."

activities.title: Reason to read

katëtan bërierind. Nda tsuun pëkuanj tsi utsia ndu fetsan-naa irim yi nduu ja yi.

they can read the story again with a partner.

Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do it.

• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "c" 5 times.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
UKAC UNTEERU NI UJUGËRI
Ukac Unteeru ni Ujugëri aci ifetsar. A nga ciina di bëko bëyampal.
Unu ulon Ukac Unteeru ja,"Ngëleemp bëcang." Maa Ujugëri ja, "Faan jakee leemp bëcang."
Unu utëbantsän, Ukac Unteeru ja, "Ngëleemp bëcang." Maa Ujugëri ja, "Faan jakee leemp bëcang."
Unu uwaajatsän, Ukac Unteeru ja, "Ngëleemp bëcang." Maa Ujugëri ja, "Faan jakee leemp bëcang."
Din, Ukac Unteeru leemp bëcang wël.
Maa Ujugëri ja ,"Faan meen leemp bëcang inji."
Unu ulon, bënu yëk mak tsi ngëkac. Ukac Unteeru yits ee niaj bëcang wël. Maa Ujugëri kaats bëcang.
Unu këfa, ufuts futs, a ufuts mak. Ukac Unteeru yits ee niaj bëcang wël kak. Maa Ujugëri kaats 
bëcang te inkri. Ufa unu kak, usubal sub, a usub mak. Ukac Unteeru yits ee niaj bëcang wël. Maa 
Ujugëri te inkri kaats bëcang.
Uunk bënu tër Ujugëri ufuts futs Ujugëri, A usubal subar Ujugëri. Maa unu un ci wi Ujugëri këja, 
"Faan mee leemp bëcang."

activities.title: Assessment: Before The Lesson
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the title 
"letters", "syllables" and "individual score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find 
the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct 
pupils who are not being assessed to read the 
story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: "Cuuca a win ne bañaan a ci tsi pëteen kako-ul. Ngëteen kafëlal par pëme ko wi bañaan 
do wi ka teen ni ko wi Cuuca ro wi.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress

• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending".

Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupil have learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with 
the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the two flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: "Përim pi apac we?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: Mán ci tsi pëwejats përim. Përim pi aci "/pëcaa/". Nda jun ngëwaaf itawar pul /pë/ /
caa/.
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Book. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 

board.
• Say: "Përim pi aci "/pëcaa/". Inkri ngëpican përim bëlieng.Nda jun ngëja pul uyaas uloole. 
(Pupils read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their 
copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the rest 
of the words.
Words: /u/ pi/ "upi" /pë//caa/ "pëjaa" /Paa/pa/ "Paapa" /bë/ /naa/na/"bënaana"
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: "Inkri, man ŋal nda roon ndu teen pëleemp irim ind bërierind.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:

the same word by themselves.

teenan itawar përim, ndu ru përim. Nda tsuun pëkuanj nda fetsanaan". (Monitor and help 
pupils.)

NAJAAR NI UBUURU
Aka Najaar na ciinee utab wi ka njakaa wi Faala. Ka leemp mak di bëreeŋul unu un ci wi.
A saal upiets a upiets jab uwar. Najaar ni aci na njuabi uwaas mak.
Ka tseend bañaan bëlieng upietsul, abofand Nasien Niints ni Nasien Ŋaats. Unu ulon, Nasien 
Niints ja, "Nda yaari upiets pur bënoonts inja."
A Najaar tsëp bëreeŋul a nee jëk ni ubuuru. Ubuuru jaul,"Bëfa Najaar."
Najaar yank wël a na ja, "Bëlon Kayëts!"
Ubuuru jaul, "Jampsan kë tsënkin këruakarin ubaca. Uko re pëtsats a ba." Najaar ja wël, "Gijin ka 
tsënku."
Ubuuru gij Najaar atukand mak përuak ubaca. Maa ubaca tuk buts mak.
Tsëkanäts pëmob wël.
A Najaar jej pëgareul a na ja, 'Taa!' Ubaca lënk a u tuk mak alawan. Ubuuru ja, "Mán tsënku ka 
yuunts upiets pëtsëpand di Nasien."
Di kato pësien, bañaan bëlieng aci ni ulilan.
Nasien ja, "Baran Ubuuru! Jampsaan këbuti kee ci tsi." Uunk, Ubuuru but ee ka tsënk bañaan.

new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the 
pupils, depending on the responses.

share the words with their families at home.

activities.title: Assessment: BEFORE THE LESSON
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment

List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the title 
"letters", "syllables" and "individual score".

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: "Aka ko wi bakaats batëb nats wi aci tsi pëteen. Ngëteen tsi katëtan nja ka me ko wi ban 
ats wink koo teenni ko un ka wi a ba ci tsi pëteen wël." 
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil

• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending"..
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupil have learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with 
the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say:"Përim pi apac we?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word. Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: "Mán ci tsi pëwejats përim. Përim pi aci "/Maama/". Nda jun ngëteen nja ka waaf itawar 
pul /maa/ /ma / "Maama".
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
•  Say: "Përim pi aci "Maama". Inkri ngëpican përim bëlieng. Nda jun ngëja pul bëlieng uyaas 
uloole". (Pupils read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their 
copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the rest 
of the words.
Words: m/ cam/, ka/bamb/, i /caa/, maa /ma/.
Use syllables to build new words
• Say: "Inkri, mán ŋal nda roon ndu teen pëleemp irim ind bërierind".
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.

read the word.
• Say: "Nda jun ngëteen wël bëlieng".

the same word by themselves.
• Say: "Inkri nda me ko wi nda ka wi përo. Nda teenan irim icints di ngëbuk ind. Ucäk, nda 
teenan itawar përim, ndu ru përim. Nda tsuun pëkuanj ndu fetsanaan".  (Monitor and help 
pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

Jonats, napats nampëli baandi,
A na te upi kërugi di bametsu pëlik. Nampëli ni toti upi di pëlik.

UCUTS NI UPI
Pëlon pënak, Upi ni Ucuts ro lofënts mak. Upi ja Ucuts, "Ngëtsëp katsas mlik përaan." Ucuts niran 
u ja, "Ucär,ngëtsëp pëtsas."
Ba yandaar, a yandaar, a yandaar. Ba tuk, a tuk, a tuk.
Utuami, ba band pëlik. Pëlik ka mlik ko utiis.
Upi ja, "Inkri, ngëka mlik përaan." Ucuts niran, "Ucär, ngëka mlik përaan." Ucuts cat a wela pëlik.
Upi cat buts a wela pëlik.
Ucuts raan mlik - uraan, araan araan. Upi raan mlik- uraan, araan, araan. Nga raan te nga tewan.
Din uband nga cili di pëlik.
Ucuts ja, "Pëlik a wand, I yilats pëcil."
Upi niran, "Ucär, pëlik a wand. I yilats buts pëcil! We wi nja këro wën?" A Ucuts ja, "Mame ko wi 
ngëka wi përo.
Man cakës jut di ufetsu ka cil. Uba ka totu ka cilan buts." Uunk ri Ucuts do ru a ucil.
Upi ruwar, "Tsëcuts-aa, m ci tsum?" Maa Ucuts tsëpba.
Jonats, napats nampëli baandi,
A na te upi kërugi di bametsu pëlik. Nampëli ni toti upi di pëlik.
Upi baran nampëli a u pën pëtsëp.
Din u win Ucuts piints a mobaa di pëgungan.
Ucuts ja wël, "Tsëpi, jampsaan, yokësin pëcär di katsuts Ka yil pëwitsës been."
Upi ja wël, "Eyoo, mán tsënku. Maa m ka pëjuk përoor ifetsaru ko uwara wi."

napats ni do wi".

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling.
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending"..
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with 
the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the two flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items aloud once. 
Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call one of 
the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down raises their 
hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.content:

book. Read the first word.

• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the

Use syllables to build new words
• Say: "Inkri, mán ŋal nda roon ndu teen pëleemp irim ind bërierind".
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.
